sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the single most important driver of predicted default, and predicted risk rises steadily as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises with it, mainly from none to one or two.
The effect of utilization grows strongly with the number of past delinquencies: it matters far more for applicants with two delinquencies than for those with none.
Higher income is associated with lower predicted risk, though income is a weak to moderate driver overall.
A longer credit history is associated with lower predicted risk, and this is also a weak to moderate driver.
A higher debt-to-income ratio increases predicted risk, but its effect is weak to moderate in size.
The data do not settle whether the number of dependents matters for predicted default.
Age and months at the current address hardly matter for the predictions.
